 Early voting in Chaves County draws voters from both parties 
 Party data presented to county commissioners shows Democrats and Republicans favored early voting while “others” leaned toward Election Day
 by 
 Terri Harber 
 1 hour ago November 18, 2026 
 Originally reported by The Roswell Daily Record 👽

 Voters completing their ballots on Nov. 3 at the polling site in the Chaves County Administrative Center. (Terri Harber, The Roswell Daily Record) 
 Terri Harber, The Roswell Daily Record — There were 15,564 voters, comprising 39.9% of the turnout, from among Chaves County’s 38,959 registered voters, as of Nov. 3. 
 Here is some data reported by Chaves County Clerk Cindy Fuller, who presented it to the Chaves County Commissioners on Nov.12, just before they certified the county election results.
 Party affiliation data showed that both Democrats and Republicans opted more often to vote early in the November election than those who identified themselves as “others.” Overall, 7,946 Chaves County voters made their selections before Election Day, and 6,747 of them cast ballots on Election Day. Another 871 absentee ballots were accepted.
 Broken down by political affiliation countywide, Democrats cast 2,072 early ballots and 1,510 on Nov. 3. Republicans numbered 4,909 early voters and 4,010 cast ballots on Election Day. Those 1,225 who were classified as “others” voted on Nov. 3, and only 965 of them were early voters.
 Four early voting polling places operated across Chaves County from Oct. 6 to 31. The Chaves County Clerk’s Office and Roswell Mall provided polling sites for early and Election Day voting. The clerk’s office served 7,296 voters and Roswell Mall enabled 3,418 voters through early voting and on Nov. 3.  
 Chaves County also registered 411 voters on Election Day.
 The Hagerman Joy Center provided a polling place for 413 voters and Dexter Schools Central Office had 356 people who voted there. Both of these sites were open for early voting and voting on Election Day. Nine other polling sites operated on Nov. 3 inside schools, churches and at the local New Mexico Game and Fish office.
 In Chaves County, 871 absentee ballots were accepted and 411 voters registered on Nov. 3.
 New Mexico’s election results are scheduled to be certified on Nov. 24.
